extract:
Jackson Browne was born on October 9, 1948, in Heidelberg, West Germany, where his father was stationed with the U.S. military, and was raised in Southern California, first in Los Angeles's Highland Park and later in Orange County. Emerging from the folk clubs of mid-1960s Los Angeles, he became one of the defining figures of the Laurel Canyon singer-songwriter movement, and he has remained active from the late 1960s into the 2020s.

As a teenager Browne briefly played with an early lineup of the Nitty Gritty Dirt Band before moving to New York, where he accompanied Nico and wrote songs she recorded, including "These Days." His reputation as a writer preceded his own records, with artists such as Tom Rush and Linda Ronstadt cutting his material. David Geffen signed him to the newly formed Asylum Records, and the 1972 debut Jackson Browne produced the hit "Doctor My Eyes" alongside "Rock Me on the Water." That same year the Eagles, his friends from the Troubadour scene, scored with "Take It Easy," a song he co-wrote with Glenn Frey.

For Everyman (1973) included his own version of "Take It Easy" and deepened his partnership with multi-instrumentalist David Lindley, whose slide guitar and fiddle became central to his sound. Late for the Sky (1974) is often cited as his most cohesive meditation on love and mortality. The Pretender (1976), produced by Jon Landau and made in the aftermath of his wife Phyllis's suicide, yielded "Here Come Those Tears Again" and the title track. Running on Empty (1977), recorded on stage, in hotel rooms, and on tour buses, became his commercial peak, featuring the title song, "The Load-Out," and a cover of "Stay." Hold Out (1980) gave him his only No. 1 album, and "Somebody's Baby" from the Fast Times at Ridgemont High soundtrack became a major hit in 1982.

The 1980s brought an increasingly political turn. Lawyers in Love (1983) carried Cold War satire, while Lives in the Balance (1986) and World in Motion (1989) took aim at U.S. policy in Central America. Browne co-founded Musicians United for Safe Energy (MUSE), which staged the 1979 No Nukes concerts with Bruce Springsteen, Bonnie Raitt, and others, and he has long supported environmental and human rights causes. I'm Alive (1993) returned to the personal terrain of his early work, followed by Looking East (1996), The Naked Ride Home (2002), and Time the Conqueror (2008).

Critics have consistently ranked Browne among the most literate songwriters of his generation, admired for confessional honesty and a moral seriousness that carried into his activism. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2004 by Springsteen and into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2007. Later studio albums include Standing in the Breach (2014) and Downhill from Everywhere (2021), and he continues to tour and campaign for environmental causes, his early catalog standing as a cornerstone of the Southern California singer-songwriter tradition.
title: Jackson Browne
